definition: The practice of tying specific claims in a model's output back to specific supporting evidence, such as source documents or citations.
details: Grounding techniques (including citation generation) help users verify AI-generated claims and are an important tool for reducing the practical harm of hallucination.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. It is the blueprint that makes everything else possible. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. That blueprint is Fine-Grained Grounding.
